extracted.intended_audience: donors and charities seeking GiveWell recommendations / philanthropic grantmakers
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for selecting and recommending charities for funding, focused on interventions (mostly in the developing world) that maximize lives saved or improved per dollar. Includes both general grantmaking criteria and additional, stricter criteria for charities designated as GiveWell 'top charities.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: We seek out charities implementing programs that have been studied rigorously and ideally repeatedly, and whose benefits we can reasonably expect to generalize to large populations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine charity-specific data to determine how well we can expect an individual charity's real-world results to correspond to results found in academic studies of programs. Recognize limits to generalizability of study results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost-effectiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: We attempt to estimate figures such as the total 'cost per life saved' or 'cost per total economic benefit to others, normalized by base income' for each of the charities we consider.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize programs that perform well on these metrics. Note that low-income people in the developing world have dramatically lower standards of living, so a given dollar can provide more meaningful benefits when targeting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Room for more funding
rubrics_metrics.description: When we consider directing funding to a program, we ask, 'What will additional funds — beyond what a charity would raise without our recommendation — enable, and what is the value of these activities?'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only direct funding where additional donations can be used quickly and effectively; we have paused directing funding to strong charities when we didn't feel they could use additional donations quickly and effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Charities must be open to our intensive investigation process and to public discussion of their track record and progress, both the good and the bad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We publish detailed reviews discussing strengths and concerns. We expect charitable partners to engage substantively and share both positive and negative developments; transparency is central to our reasoning and public critique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant prior funding and operational observation (top-charity requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: We've directed a single grant to it of at least $10 million or multiple grants totaling at least $20 million, and we've supported the program as carried out by the implementing organization for at least one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting these thresholds is a sign of confidence: significant, sustained support implies thorough prior analysis and reduces the likelihood that future information will dramatically update cost-effectiveness assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: High likelihood of substantial impact (degree + certainty) (top-charity requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: We think there's a high likelihood of substantial impact from funding this program (as opposed to lower likelihood of enormous impact). This criterion is a function of both degree of impact and certainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A possibility of very large impact alone is insufficient; we require both expected magnitude and reasonably high probability. Deciding whether a program meets this depends on judgment calls; we commit to transparency about that reasoning. Opportunities with high expected value but low certainty may be funded via other funds, not the Top Charities Fund.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary emphasis on direct implementation impact (top-charity preference)
rubrics_metrics.description: Typically, the overwhelming case for funding rests on the direct impact of a grant, not on the value of information we might gather through it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While we may fund scoping, research, and evaluation (and have examples), the Top Charities Fund should primarily support program implementation; grants whose main value is information are often funded from a different portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific funding gaps must meet current cost-effectiveness bar
rubrics_metrics.description: The program has funding gaps that meet our current cost-effectiveness bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We look for specific opportunities within the program where we believe our funding will be deployed cost-effectively. As of July 2022, a program must be estimated at 10 times as cost-effective as unconditional cash transfers to receive our funding recommendation. We apply the same cost-effectiveness bar to opportunities evaluated outside our top charities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of significant qualitative concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are significant qualitative concerns that could jeopardize the program's success, we may choose not to list a program even if it meets the above criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of significant qualitative concerns include (but are not limited to): financial instability; changes in leadership or strategy that raise questions about continued adherence to criteria; instances in which the organization discovers illicit or fraudulent activities and does not take swift, comprehensive corrective actions aligned with best practices and its own policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on priority programs and developing-world direct aid
rubrics_metrics.description: We focus on programs in the developing world and on interventions for which there is strong independent evidence of effectiveness, particularly direct aid (e.g., distributing bed nets, deworming, malaria prevention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: GiveWell narrowed its scope because developing-world programs generally had more robust evidence bases and considerably lower per-person costs, yielding a stronger case for accomplishing more good per dollar. Root-causes or speculative long-term approaches are typically deprioritized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intensive evaluation process and ongoing follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Our intensive evaluation process aims to deeply and critically question the case for the charity's impact, and we follow up intensively with our top charities over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: We publicly lay out strengths and weaknesses, engage substantively with top charities, conduct lookbacks comparing outcomes to original assessments, and use ongoing engagement as a major argument for supporting charities (because top charities are generally willing to engage given the scale of donations directed to them).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and application pathways
rubrics_metrics.description: We conduct extensive searches for charities that focus on our priority programs and invite promising charities to apply for a GiveWell recommendation; charities may also contact us to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility starts with focusing on GiveWell's priority programs. Being proactive in engaging with GiveWell and providing the data needed for intensive review is part of the practical pathway to consideration.
